arxiv-1905-07581.title: Convolutional Feature Extraction and Neural Arithmetic Logic Units for Stock Prediction
arxiv-1905-07581.creator: Shangeth Rajaa, Jajati Keshari Sahoo
arxiv-1905-07581.description: Abstract Stock prediction is a topic undergoing intense study for many years. Finance experts and mathematicians have been working on a way to predict the future stock price so as to decide to buy the stock or sell it to make profit.

arxiv-2011-08086.title: A Note on Projective Modules
arxiv-2011-08086.creator: Hossein Faridian
arxiv-2011-08086.description: Abstract . This expository note delves into the theory of projective modules parallel to the one developed for injective modules by Matlis. Given a perfect ring R R , we present a characterization of indecomposable projective R R -modules and describe a one-to-one correspondence between the projective indecomposable R R -modules and the simple R R -modules.

arxiv-2101-08611.title: General Decidability Results for Asynchronous Shared-Memory Programs: Higher-Order and Beyond
arxiv-2101-08611.creator: Rupak Majumdar, Ramanathan S. Thinniyam, Georg Zetzsche
arxiv-2101-08611.description: Abstract . The model of asynchronous programming arises in many contexts, from low-level systems software to high-level web programming. We take a language-theoretic perspective and show general decidability and undecidability results for asynchronous programs that capture all known results as well as show decidability of new and important classes.

arxiv-2208-10652.title: Learning Visibility for Robust Dense Human Body Estimation
arxiv-2208-10652.creator: Chun-Han Yao 1 Jimei Yang 2 Duygu Ceylan 2 Yi Zhou 2, Yang Zhou 2 Ming-Hsuan Yang 134
arxiv-2208-10652.description: Abstract Estimating 3D human pose and shape from 2D images is a crucial yet challenging task. While prior methods with model-based representations can perform reasonably well on whole-body images, they often fail when parts of the body are occluded or outside the frame.

arxiv-2506-11500.title: A note on intrinsic topologies of groups Thanks: The research of the first named author was funded in whole by the Austrian Science Fund FWF [10.55776/ESP399].
arxiv-2506-11500.creator: S. Bardyla, L. Elliott, J. D. Mitchell, and Y. Péresse
arxiv-2506-11500.description: Abstract . We investigate topologies on groups which arise naturally from their algebraic structure, including the Frechét-Markov, Hausdorff-Markov, and various kinds of Zariski topologies. Answering a question by Dikranjan and Toller, we show that there exists a countable abelian group in which no bounded version of the Zariski topology coincides with the full Zariski topology.

arxiv-2508-12411.title: The Cultural Gene of Large Language Models: A Study on the Impact of Cross-Corpus Training on Model Values and Biases
arxiv-2508-12411.creator: Emanuel Z. Fenech-Borg, Tilen P. Meznaric-Kos, Milica D. Lekovic-Bojovic, Arni J. Hentze-Djurhuus
arxiv-2508-12411.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Emanuel Z. Fenech-Borg, Tilen P. Meznaric-Kos, Milica D. Lekovic-Bojovic, Arni J. Hentze-Djurhuus. Large Language Models (LLMs) are being deployed globally, yet their underlying cultural and ethical assumptions remain underexplored. This paper investigates the concept of "cultural genes"—systematic value orientations that LLMs inherit from their training corpora. We introduce a novel methodology centered on a Cultural Probe Dataset (CPD) designed to evaluate models along key cross-cultural psychological dimensions, specifically Individualism-Collectivism (IDV) and Power Distance (PDI).

arxiv-2509-01205.title: Neutrino phenomenology and Dark matter in a left-right asymmetric model with non-holomorphic modular A 4 A_{4} group Journal: Physics Letters B
arxiv-2509-01205.creator: Bhabana Kumar, Mrinal Kumar Das
arxiv-2509-01205.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bhabana Kumar, Mrinal Kumar Das. We present a model constructed within a non-supersymmetric framework capable of explaining both current neutrino oscillation data and the observed dark matter relic abundance. In this study, the Yukawa couplings are expressed as polyharmonic Maaß forms, and the non-supersymmetric left-right symmetric model is realized through the Γ 3 \Gamma_{3} modular group, with neutrino masses generated via the Type II seesaw dominance mechanism.

arxiv-2601-12505.title: DoPE : Decoy Oriented Perturbation Encapsulation Human-Readable, AI-Hostile Documents for Academic Integrity
arxiv-2601-12505.creator: Ashish Raj Shekhar, Shiven Agarwal, Priyanuj Bordoloi, Yash Shah, Vivek Gupta
arxiv-2601-12505.description: Abstract Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can directly consume exam documents, threatening conventional assessments and academic integrity. We present DoPE (Decoy-Oriented Perturbation Encapsulation), a document-layer defense framework that embeds semantic decoys into PDF/HTML assessments to exploit render–parse discrepancies in MLLM pipelines.

arxiv-2602-07005.title: Admittance-Based Motion Planning with Vision-Guided Initialization for Robotic Manipulators in Self-Driving Laboratories
arxiv-2602-07005.creator: Shifa Sulaiman*, Tobias Jensen, Francesco Schetter, Simon Bøgh
arxiv-2602-07005.description: Abstract Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) represent highly automated research environments that leverage advanced technologies to conduct experiments and analyze data with minimal human involvement. SDLs often involve delicate laboratory equipment, unexpected environmental interactions, and occasional human intervention, which makes compliant and force-aware control essential for ensuring safety, adaptability, and reliability.

pmc-10599535.title: The acoustical behavior of a bass guitar bridge with no saddles
pmc-10599535.creator: Jonathan A. Kemp, Khalil Abdelrazek Khalil, Khalil Abdelrazek Khalil, Khalil Abdelrazek Khalil
pmc-10599535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The acoustics of a bass guitar bridge without saddles was tested experimentally and the results contextualised. pmc-13460900.title: Digital health promotion strategies to increase HIV testing uptake among key populations: a scoping review
pmc-13460900.creator: Syamikar Baridwan Syamsir, T. Widya Naralia, Hesti Rahayu, Eny Dewi Pamungkas, Raphita Diorarta, Agus Setiawan, Rian Adi Pamungkas, Zainuddin Zainuddin
pmc-13460900.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). :HIV testing uptake among key populations remains suboptimal despite its central role in HIV prevention. Digital health promotion strategies have been increasingly implemented to address multilevel barriers to testing. However, current evidence is fragmented across platforms, populations, and settings. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize current evidence on digital health promotion strategies designed to increase HIV testing uptake among key populations. This scoping review adopted Arksey & O’Malley’s five-stage framework and reported the process following PRISMA-ScR.
